standard_prerequisites.name: Derivations across the normalization at nodes
standard_prerequisites.use: Transports a derivation D on X to a derivation D' on the normalization X^nu whose behaviour at the preimages of nodes mirrors D.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of derivations on smooth projective curves
standard_prerequisites.use: Part (1) kills derivations on components of genus > 1, part (2) on genus-1 components fixing a point, part (3) on rational components fixing three points.

standard_prerequisites.name: The excluded configurations
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Examples example-rational-tail and example-rational-bridge
standard_prerequisites.use: Rule out the low-node configurations that would let a rational or elliptic component survive with a nonzero derivation.

core_obligations: Transport (proof lines 6968-6972): D corresponds to D' on the normalization via the nodal vector-field correspondence.
Components of genus > 1 (proof lines 6973-6975): D'|_{O_C} = 0 by part (1) of the smooth vector-field lemma.

Components of genus 1 (proof lines 6976-6983): some closed point of C maps to a node of X, since otherwise X would be the genus-1 curve C itself; the correspondence makes D' fix that point, so D'|_{O_C} = 0 by part (2).

Rational components (proof lines 6984-6995): at least three pairwise distinct closed points of C map to nodes, since with fewer one obtains two glued points, a rational bridge, or a rational tail, all excluded by the genus and no-tail no-bridge hypotheses; fixing three points forces D'|_{O_C} = 0 by part (3).
proof_roadmap: Move the derivation to the normalization via the node correspondence.
Kill it on components of genus at least 1 using the fixed-node property.
Force three fixed points on rational components by excluding the glued, bridge, and tail configurations.
Apply the three-point vanishing on the projective line and conclude D' = 0, hence D = 0.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves vanishing of the tangent space Der_k(O_X, O_X) for stable nodal curves (statement lines 6959-6966). The proof (lines 6968-6995) is a complete three-case component analysis: genus > 1 components by the smooth-curve vanishing, genus 1 components via the forced node fixed by the correspondence, and rational components via the exclusion of the two-glued-points, rational-bridge, and rational-tail configurations leaving three fixed points. Every step is present with no omissions. H3: the exclusion argument forcing three marked points on rational components is a genuine geometric rigidity argument, and the lemma is the chapter's capstone.
